planting.note: Plant divisions or potted stock in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Set out container-grown plants at the same depth they were growing in the nursery pot, spacing them wide enough to show off the large, flecked blooms. Mulch lightly with leaf litter to keep roots cool and moisten the crown without burying it. Expect abundant, large single cream flowers heavily flecked and splashed with strawberry-red beginning in late winter. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before new bloom stalks emerge to keep the clump tidy.

planting.note: Install in fall or early spring in evenly moist, well-drained shade soil enriched with compost.

directions: Grow in a shaded border with reliable winter moisture, since this vigorous strain can carry fifty or more blooms per mature clump. Flowers open bright white with freckled magenta-pink veining and picotee edges, each bloom carrying a slightly different pattern. Deadheading is unnecessary since the papery sepals persist and keep their color for weeks after pollination. Divide congested clumps in late summer once the evergreen foliage has had a full season to recover from bloom.

planting.note: Transplant in fall or early spring into rich, humusy soil beneath deciduous shade, where it will receive bright winter light before the canopy leafs out.

directions: Plant where the fully double, ruffled blooms can be viewed up close, since each flower blends white and deep magenta-pink tones around creamy yellow stamens. This selection is especially floriferous on established four-year clumps, so allow generous spacing for the bushy, dark-green foliage to mature undisturbed. Water during dry spells in its first autumn and spring while roots establish, then rely on natural rainfall once settled. Trim away winter-worn leaves in late winter just as new flower stems begin to rise.

planting.note: Site in dappled to full shade with consistently moist, organically rich soil; plant in fall or early spring for best establishment.

directions: Use this near-black double hellebore as a dramatic accent against lighter-flowered companions, since its velvety, deep purple-black blooms carry pale yellow stamens that glow by contrast. The heavily layered petals give each flower roughly triple the petal count of a single-form hellebore and hold their rich color for weeks after pollination finishes. Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged, particularly during the first growing season. Cut back old, weathered leaves in late winter before the new bloom stalks elongate.

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in well-drained, compost-enriched soil under high, open shade.

directions: Choose this pink double selection for a softer counterpart to darker Winter Thrillers cultivars, since its fluffy, cup-shaped blooms range from light blush to bright lipstick pink, some lightly speckled with purple. New foliage unfurls a rich mahogany shade in spring before maturing to leathery dark green, giving multi-season structure after bloom. The persistent papery sepals hold color for weeks, so there is no need to deadhead for tidiness. Divide only when clumps become crowded, as hellebores resent frequent disturbance.
